findings.title: cheapestFirst sorts the shared cached catalog in place, which breaks 'newest' on every later page load
findings.scenario: loadCatalog stores one catalog object in the module-level `cache` and hands that same object to every caller. On the first homePage(catalog) call, `newest` is computed first and is correct. Then featuredDeals sorts catalog.items by price in place. finding.title: The sort comparator returns a boolean, so topPlayers does not reliably put the highest scores first

findings.title: The sort comparator returns a boolean, so topPlayers does not reliably put the highest scores first
findings.scenario: Array.prototype.sort expects a negative, zero, or positive number. This comparator returns true or false, which become 1 or 0, and never a negative value. So when a should come before b, the result is 0 ('equal') and the pair is not reordered. Example: board [{player:'A',points:5},{player:'B',points:1},{player:'C',points:9}] gives a merge step where C:9 never moves ahead of A:5 because comparing them returns 0. The result is [A:5, B:1, C:9] instead of [C:9, A:5, B:1]. The top-players list, which is the requested feature, comes out wrong for any input that is not already sorted.
findings.whyNotPrevented: There are no tests in the repo (Glob **/*.{test,spec}.js found nothing). Plain JS has no type checking, so a boolean comparator is accepted without error.
